source.objectiveEnglish: Say where you are going, what the crew is going to do, and what you can do.
source.focusSpanish: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer and poder for jobsite tasks
source.speakingEnglish: Tell a coworker where you are going now, what the crew is going to do tomorrow, and one task you can do.

archivedDraft.title: Find a person or a tool
archivedDraft.scene: Sato and Kobayashi locate Tanaka, Yamada, and Sato's hammer before the shift starts
materialDrift: Older Japanese Foundation 5 teaches finding people and tools with Sato and Kobayashi; the source teaches Rosa and Miguel's work plans, materials, and certified forklift use.

cards.sourceNoteInternal: Common Mexican term; some crews say la forma.

cards.sourceEnglish: I'm going to the hardware store.

cards.sourceSpanish: Vamos a colar el concreto mañana.
cards.sourceEnglish: We're going to pour the concrete tomorrow.
cards.sourceNoteInternal: Colar is the common Mexican verb for pouring concrete; echar also works.
cards.japaneseDraft: 明日、コンクリートを打設します。

cards.sourceSpanish: Ellos van a hacer la cimbra.
cards.sourceEnglish: They're going to build the formwork.
cards.japaneseDraft: あの人たちは型枠を組みます。

cards.sourceSpanish: Yo puedo manejar el montacargas; tengo certificación.
cards.sourceEnglish: I can drive the forklift; I'm certified.
cards.japaneseDraft: 私はフォークリフトを運転できます。資格を持っています。

cards.sourceEnglish: Juan is going to the roof.
cards.japaneseDraft: フアンは屋根に行きます。

reader.sourceSpanish: En la obra, Rosa le dice a Miguel: Voy a la ferretería.
reader.sourceEnglish: At the site, Rosa tells Miguel: I'm going to the hardware store.
reader.japaneseDraft: 現場で、ローサはミゲルに言います。「金物店に行きます。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Miguel: Yo voy a la bodega por una pala.
reader.sourceEnglish: Miguel: I'm going to the storage area for a shovel.
reader.japaneseDraft: ミゲル：「シャベルを取りに資材置き場へ行きます。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Miguel: La cuadrilla va a excavar la zanja hoy.
reader.sourceEnglish: Miguel: The crew is going to dig the trench today.
reader.japaneseDraft: ミゲル：「作業班は今日、掘削溝を掘ります。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Rosa: Vamos a colar el concreto mañana.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rosa: We're going to pour the concrete tomorrow.
reader.japaneseDraft: ローサ：「明日、コンクリートを打設します。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Rosa: Ellos van a hacer la cimbra para el piso.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rosa: They're going to build the formwork for the floor.

reader.sourceSpanish: Rosa: Hacemos la mezcla a las 8.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rosa: We make the mix at 8.

reader.sourceSpanish: Miguel: Yo puedo manejar el montacargas; tengo certificación.
reader.sourceEnglish: Miguel: I can drive the forklift; I'm certified.
reader.japaneseDraft: ミゲル：「私はフォークリフトを運転できます。資格を持っています。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Rosa: Juan va al techo con su arnés.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rosa: Juan is going to the roof with his harness.
reader.japaneseDraft: ローサ：「フアンはハーネスを着けて屋根に行きます。」

reader.sourceSpanish: Rosa: El baño portátil va junto a la bodega.
reader.sourceEnglish: Rosa: The porta-potty goes next to the storage area.
reader.japaneseDraft: ローサ：「仮設トイレは資材置き場の隣です。」

decisionsNeeded: Resolve whether source floor/piso means the slab, a storey, or the finished floor in cards 7 and Reader 5 before selecting a Japanese term.
Resolve what mixture the source calls la mezcla in card 8, card 14 and Reader 6, despite card 8's parenthetical mortar gloss.
Review Japanese construction terms for formwork, trench, concrete placement and forklift certification; preserve source attribution rather than asserting a universal site rule.
Adapt ir/ir a, hacer and poder to natural Japanese plans, action and ability; do not copy Spanish conjugation teaching.
Author six actual mode prompt/target pairs, forms, speaking, dictionary and saved-item mapping before learner use.
